deferred_v2: Drive API markdown bridge (CreateDocFromMarkdown / ExportDocAsMarkdown) — base www.googleapis.com, scopes already cover it
Remaining batchUpdate niceties only if needed
design_note_index_free_rework: Text and Paragraph components no longer take document indices. Every one authors its request(s) at a placeholder index (1) and outputs a list. Real placement happens only in ArrangeContentComponent (renamed from AppendCursorComponent, now in the Combine tab), which is now the mandatory hub every block passes through before RequestAggregatorComponent. Insert / Structure tabs are unchanged and still take raw indices — they reference either fresh placeholder positions or genuinely pre-existing document structure (named ranges) that can't be stacked the same way.
design_note_table_tab_rework: The Table tab's original 5 components (InsertTableRow/InsertTableColumn/DeleteTableRow/DeleteTableColumn/MergeTableCells) were removed entirely per user decision: editing an existing table's rows/columns/cells requires live structural indices pulled from a fetched document, which isn't a realistic thing to hand-author in a Grasshopper workflow. TableRequestBuilders.cs (their only builder) was deleted as dead code. Data Tree To Table and Fixed Size Table moved here from the removed Report Tools tab, since building a table FROM data is the realistic table-authoring pattern. The Report Tools tab itself was dissolved — its remaining components redistributed to the tabs they align with: Report Skeleton / Report Header Block / Bullet List went to Paragraph (they're paragraph-style composites), and Arrange Content went to Combine (it feeds directly into Request Aggregator).
design_note_segment_content: Google Docs gives headers/footers/footnotes their own separate index space (a 'segment') — inserting text into one needs location.segmentId (the ID returned by the createHeader/createFooter/createFootnote reply), not a body index. The ONLY part that genuinely needs a live API round-trip is obtaining that ID — it's server-generated and unknowable before the create request executes. Everything after that is a plain request object like any other. So: Create Header / Create Footer / Create Footnote are live write components (Document tab) that create the segment AND take an optional Text input — if filled, they immediately insert that plain text into the segment as a one-step convenience (create, read back the ID, insertText, all in the same component); if left blank, they just create the empty segment. Either way they return the Header ID / Footer ID / Footnote ID, so richer content (bold, multiple lines, alignment, mixed styling) can still be layered in afterward: every Text-tab and Paragraph-tab component has an optional 'Segment ID' input (blank = body) — wiring the returned ID into it targets that segment with the exact same self-indexed-from-1 model already used for body content. Multiple blocks going into the same segment still need Arrange Content to sequence them — just a SEPARATE Arrange Content instance per segment (body vs. each header/footer/footnote), since their index spaces are independent and mixing them in one Arrange Content run would cross-contaminate the content-length tally. 'Header Type'/'Footer Type' is dropped as a user input entirely: Google's HeaderFooterType enum only supports "DEFAULT" for creation (odd/even/first-page headers are controlled separately via document style flags, not this field), so it's hardcoded rather than exposed. SharedBuilders.Location/Range gain an optional segmentId parameter (default null = body); every existing call site is unaffected since it passes null.

components.note: Fetches by Document ID, or resolves a Name to an ID via the Drive API (files.list) then fetches. Name lookup needs a Drive-scoped token (drive.readonly / drive.metadata.readonly); drive.file only sees app-created files.

outputs.name: Document ID
outputs.note: The ID actually used (resolved from Name when looked up); chains into Batch Update / Clear Document / Create Header / Create Footer / Create Footnote.

components.note: Composes get_document + batch_update_document internally (does not consume the Requests JSON payload contract — same precedent as CreateDocument/GetDocument). Full-document clear only, no partial range. Fetches the doc's real body end index via get_document, then issues one deleteContentRange(1, bodyEnd-1) — index 1 can't be deleted (implicit trailing newline).

MOVED from Structure + EDITED (revised again — see design_note_segment_content). Live write: (1) batchUpdate createHeader (type hardcoded DEFAULT — 'Header Type' dropped as a user input), parse the returned Header ID; (2) if Text is non-blank, batchUpdate insertText of Text into that segment in the same step — a one-component convenience for the simple case. Text left blank just creates the empty segment; either way, Header ID is returned so richer content (bold, multiple lines, alignment) can be layered in afterward via any Text/Paragraph-tab component's Segment ID input. Does not consume the Requests JSON payload contract for its own create call (same precedent as Clear Document) — but content added later via Segment ID does flow through the normal contract.

MOVED from Structure + EDITED, same pattern as Create Header. Live write: creates the DEFAULT footer segment; if Text is non-blank, also inserts it into the segment in the same step. Text left blank just creates the empty segment. Footer ID is always returned for layering richer content afterward via any Text/Paragraph-tab component's Segment ID input.

MOVED from Structure + EDITED, same pattern. Index is kept (unlike Text/Paragraph tabs) because it anchors the footnote marker to a specific point in the main body — a body-position reference, not a stackable content block, consistent with other Structure-tab components like Create Named Range. Creates the footnote reference via batchUpdate createFootnote at Index; if Text is non-blank, also inserts it into the footnote's segment in the same step. Footnote ID is always returned for layering richer content afterward via Segment ID.

subcategories.name: Table
subcategories.note: REWORKED. The 5 low-level row/column/merge editors (InsertTableRow/InsertTableColumn/DeleteTableRow/DeleteTableColumn/MergeTableCells) were removed entirely per user decision — they require live table-structure indices from a fetched document, which isn't a realistic GH-workflow authoring pattern. TableRequestBuilders.cs (their sole builder) was deleted as dead code. The tab now holds the two components that actually build a table from data, moved here from the removed Report Tools tab.

components.note: MOVED from Report Tools (tab removed). Composite: one InsertTable + index-sequenced cell InsertText requests, self-indexed from 1; optional bold header row. Table shape is inferred from the tree (branch count = rows, items per branch = columns). For explicit Rows/Columns control, use Fixed Size Table instead.

MOVED from Report Tools (tab removed). Same composite pattern as Data Tree To Table, but table shape is explicit (Rows x Columns) instead of inferred. If the data tree has fewer cells than Rows x Columns, remaining cells are left blank; if more, extras are dropped with a runtime warning. Self-indexed from 1.

subcategories.name: Structure
subcategories.note: Create Header / Create Footer / Create Footnote live in Document (http) — see design_note_segment_content. Only pure JSON units (no live API calls) remain here.

subcategories.name: Combine
subcategories.note: Request Aggregator is the single placement-and-gathering hub every self-indexed block passes through (it absorbed the former Arrange Content on 2026-09-13; that component has since been deleted).

components.note: ABSORBED Arrange Content (2026-09-13). Now the single placement-and-gathering hub: reads each wire into Request JSON as its own block (one further sub-block per branch), re-indexes them in wire order from Start Index by tallying content length, then appends Fixed Requests verbatim. Request JSON stays at parameter index 0 so saved definitions keep their wires. Run one instance per index space (body, or each header/footer/footnote).

Unlike the other presets, Font Family is NOT a closed API enum — any installed font name string is valid. This is a curated shortcut list, not validation; Font Family inputs remain plain free-text and can still be typed directly.

payload_contracts.note: create_document uses a separate Title-only shape (API genuinely differs). Clear Document, Create Header, Create Footer, and Create Footnote each compose their own get/create + batch_update calls internally and do not consume this contract either — same precedent. Note the distinction: Create Header/Footer/Footnote's OWN create-segment call is separate, but the header/footer/footnote CONTENT (built with ordinary Text/Paragraph components + their Segment ID input) flows through the normal Requests JSON contract like any body content.

aec_features_not_selected.name: PageStamp
aec_features_not_selected.reason: Deferred — confirmed there is genuinely no 'Page X of Y' field anywhere in the Docs API request set (not a design choice, an API limitation). Now that headers/footers can hold text (this pass), a footer can carry a STATIC string like "Page 1", but there is no auto-incrementing token the API exposes.
